key_insight: PrivMeSA lets a local clinical agent decide what to share with remote LLMs while learning to minimize privacy risk and still reuse expert guidance in future cases.
clinical_relevance: This could support safer clinical decision support workflows where patient data exposure must be tightly controlled during multi-turn model collaboration.
method: Local agent handles each encounter and consults remote specialists only when needed.
Reinforcement learning balances task accuracy against disclosure and registry-based re-identification risk across the full outbound transcript.
A local lesson memory distills completed consultations into generalized guidance so future cases can reuse expertise without another remote exchange.
evidence_signal: On an emergency-department benchmark from MIMIC-IV-ED, PrivMeSA improved mean task accuracy by up to 15.8 percentage points while reducing personal-detail disclosure from 98.0% to 0.2% of cases.
watch_item: Results come from a benchmark setting, so real-world performance, governance, and safety will depend on local deployment rules, registry assumptions, and careful validation.
paper_title: PrivMeSA: Privacy-Aware Self-Evolving Multi-Agent System for Medicine via Local-Remote LLM Collaboration
